questions.prompt: A pupil is making a card for this theme. Under the heading "a library growing stronger" she has written four words of lesson 23. One of the four says the opposite of that heading and has to come off the card. Which one?
questions.explanation: "shortage" is the word to take off: a shortage is the situation of not having enough of something, and a library that is growing stronger is precisely the library that no longer has one. "expansion" is the growing itself, so it names the heading rather than contradicting it. "literacy" is the ability to read and write, which is what a library exists to spread. And "crafts" are the skills of the hand, pottery, weaving, carpentry, which the lesson puts in the same list as science and mathematics: a growing library carries books on them too. Note that this last one says nothing good or bad by itself, so valuing the four words will not sort them; only one of them names a lack, and a lack is the opposite of growth.

questions.prompt: Hedi went to the school library at one o'clock and found the door shut. He tells his class: "I looked through the window and there weren't ___ pupils inside." Which word fills the gap?
questions.explanation: "any" is the word: the verb is already negative, weren't, and after a negative verb English uses any, not some. "some" belongs to affirmative statements, and putting it after weren't is the commonest mistake of this lesson. "no" would mark the negative a second time: English says either there weren't any pupils or there were no pupils, and never both at once. "none" is a pronoun, which means it stands alone and never comes in front of a noun; you can say there were none inside, but not none pupils.

questions.prompt: A poster on the wall of a reading club in El Kef begins with these words: "The longer you keep a library open, ___". Which ending finishes the poster in correct English?

options.text: the more families they use it.

questions.explanation: "the more families use it." completes the pattern: parallel change is built out of two comparatives, and the second half needs its own the in front of its own comparative, exactly like the first. "the most families use it." replaces the comparative by a superlative, which ranks one item above all the others instead of tying two movements together. "more families use it." drops the the of the second half, and without it the two halves are no longer linked; the sentence reads as two separate statements. And "the more families they use it." adds the pronoun they after a subject that is already there, families, so the clause carries its subject twice.

questions.prompt: Emna reached the music shop in Bizerte five minutes after closing time. She rang, she waited, she looked through the glass: the lights were off and the till was empty. She writes to her brother: "___ was still there." Which word fits?
questions.explanation: "Nobody" is the word she needs: it carries the negative itself, so the verb after it stays affirmative, and Nobody was still there says exactly what she saw. "Somebody" belongs to affirmative statements and says the opposite of an empty shop. "Anybody" cannot open a statement with this meaning: in an affirmative sentence any and its compounds mean practically every one, so Anybody was still there would say that everybody was in the shop. And "Not anybody" is the shape a learner reaches for when the negative has to come first; English never begins a sentence that way, it either moves the negative into the verb, there wasn't anybody, or into the word, nobody.

questions.prompt: Read this short piece from a school magazine in Nabeul, then answer. "Since the town's music shop closed in 2021, the record club has met in the back room of a cafe. Its twelve members bring their own players. Last month they counted forty-one visitors, against nine in their first month. Two of them now run a Saturday show on a local radio, and the club has been asked to open a second evening." What can you safely conclude from this piece?

options.text: The town's music shop reopened after 2021 and took the club back.
The Saturday radio show was created before the music shop closed.
The club is growing, and other people now want more of it.
The club's twelve members are the only people who ever come.

questions.explanation: "The club is growing, and other people now want more of it." is the only safe conclusion: forty-one visitors against nine is growth, and being asked to open a second evening is a demand that comes from outside the club. "The town's music shop reopened after 2021 and took the club back." contradicts the first sentence, which says the club has met in the cafe ever since the shop closed. "The Saturday radio show was created before the music shop closed." invents a date the piece never gives; the word now is all it says about the show. And "The club's twelve members are the only people who ever come." confuses two different figures: twelve is the number of members, forty-one the number of visitors, and the piece counts them separately for that reason.
